title: Completed extension-by-zero base change
statement:
Let $(A,I)$ satisfy [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], and let
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
U'&\xrightarrow{g_U}&U\\
j'\downarrow&&\downarrow j\\
X'&\xrightarrow{g}&X
\end{array}
$$
be a cartesian open-immersion square [def-cbc-open-immersion-square]. Assume in addition that $j$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Use the completed coefficient sheaves $A_T=\varprojlim_n(A/I^n)_T$ and $D(T_{\Proet},A)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))$ of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Identify $A_X|_U=A_U$ and $A_{X'}|_{U'}=A_{U'}$ under the slice-site identifications [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. Extension by zero $j_!$ and $j'_!$ means sheafification of the extension-by-zero module presheaf on these ringed slice sites [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], applied termwise to complexes. Let $K\in D(U_{\Proet},A)$ be derived $I$-complete [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion]. Then $j_!K$ is derived $I$-complete, and the canonical completed base-change map
$$
Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}j_!K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }j'_!Lg_{U,\mathrm{comp}}^*K
$$
is an isomorphism, natural in $K$, where completed pullback is [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Both sides belong to the derived $I$-complete subcategory of $D(X'_{\Proet},A)$. The canonical map is the one induced by the finite-coefficient extension-by-zero base-change maps and the comparison between extension by zero and the derived limit of the strict reduction tower.

proof.text: For $e=j,j\prime$, slice localization and sectionwise limits identify the completed rings and all quotient projections on the open. Base change makes $j\prime$ quasi-compact. Extension is exact and $A$-linear. Extend one flat-term K-flat representative by the flat-resolution lemma; the augmented strict-reduction lemma gives $\rho_e:(e_!K)_\bullet\cong e_!K_\bullet$, with quotient actions, transitions and units.

source.place: Finite reduction, Koszul completeness, and derived-limit assembly; explicit workload re-split of 2026-10-21.

proof.text: The ringed product theorem gives the canonical product comparison for each $e_!$. Countable products are exact on both sites. Apply the exact-product strict-limit theorem to obtain $\lambda_e:e_!R\lim M_\bullet\cong R\lim e_!M_\bullet$, in its normalized Roos coordinates and respecting every strict augmentation.

source.place: Finite reduction, Koszul completeness, and derived-limit assembly; explicit workload re-split of 2026-10-21.

proof.text: Apply the exact-linear Koszul-fiber theorem to $F=e_!$ and the generators of $I$. Its hypotheses hold by Steps 1-2; the fiber and unit are precisely those defining intrinsic completeness. Thus $e_!$ preserves completeness. First apply this to $K$; completed-pullback reduction now applies to $j_!K$ for $g$ and to $K$ for $g_U$. Applying preservation for $j\prime$ to the latter output proves every endpoint completeness assertion.

source.place: Finite reduction, Koszul completeness, and derived-limit assembly; explicit workload re-split of 2026-10-21.

proof.text: Apply $G_g$ to $\rho_j$ from Step 1 and follow it by the completed-ring strict finite exchange $b_K$. This gives an isomorphism $G_g((j_!K)_\bullet)\cong j\prime_!G_{g_U}(K_\bullet)$ of actual strict derived towers, whose finite components are the specified exchanges and whose inverses respect every quotient transition.

source.place: Finite reduction, Koszul completeness, and derived-limit assembly; explicit workload re-split of 2026-10-21.

proof.text: Apply functorial $R\lim$ to Step 4 and follow it by $\lambda_{j\prime}^{-1}$ from Step 2. The completed-pullback definition identifies its endpoints with $Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}j_!K$ and $j\prime_!Lg^*_{U,\mathrm{comp}}K$. This is exactly the specified finite-exchange/limit comparison and is natural. The augmented reduction comparison, normalized $\lambda$, and the presentation-transport unit equation preserve its canonical quotient units. Step 3 proves both endpoints complete.
